    98	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #kwTag(N:String) => kwV(N, V) ... </k>
    99	       requires notBool isKwV(V)
   100	  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
   101	  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
   102	  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]

   104	  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
   105	  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
   106	  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
   107	  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
   108	  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
   109	  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
   110	  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
   111	  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)

   113	  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
   114	  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
   115	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>

   117	  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)

   119	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
   120	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
   121	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)

   124	  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
   125	  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
   126	  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
   127	  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>

   129	  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
   130	  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
   131	  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
   132	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
   133	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   134	       requires X in_keys(M)
   135	  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
   136	  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
   137	  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
   138	  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
   139	  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
   140	  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
   141	  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
   142	  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
   143	  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
   144	  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
   145	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
   146	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   147	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
   148	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
   149	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
   150	        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
   151	       [priority(40)]
   152	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
   153	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
   154	       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))

     3	module MPY-CONTROLS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE

     7	
     8	  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
     9	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    10	       <env> L:Int </env>
    11	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    12	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
    13	       <env> L:Int </env>
    14	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    15	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    16	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    17	        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
    18	       [priority(40)]
    19	
    20	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    21	       <env> L:Int </env>
    22	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
    23	       requires X in_keys(M)
    24	  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
    25	  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
    26	  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).

    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]

     4	module MPY-INT
     5	  imports MPY-CORE
     6	
     7	  rule applyUn("-", I:Int) => 0 -Int I
     8	
     9	  rule applyBin("+",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 +Int I2
    10	  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
    11	  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    12	  rule applyBin("+",  B:Bool, I:Int) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi +Int I
    13	  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2
    14	  rule applyBin("*",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 *Int I2
    15	  rule applyBin("%",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => pyMod(I1, I2)
    16	  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
    17	  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0
    18	
    19	  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
    20	  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2

    22	  rule applyCmp("<",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <Int  I2
    23	  rule applyCmp("<=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <=Int I2
    24	  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
    25	  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
    26	  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
    27	  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2

     1	// reference/src/semantics/bool.k — MPY-BOOL
     2	// Bool operator cases + the truthy boolean operations (not / and / or; and-or are
     3	// value-returning short-circuit over any Vals, per Python).
     4	
     5	module MPY-BOOL
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	
     8	  rule applyUn("not", V:Val) => notBool truthy(V)
     9	
    10	  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
    11	  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2
    12	
    13	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
    14	  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
    15	  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
    16	  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
    17	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    18	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    19	       requires truthy(V)
    20	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    21	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    22	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    23	       requires truthy(V)
    24	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    25	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    26	
    27	  // ==== heap-object head: decide truthiness THROUGH the heap, never rewrite the
    28	  // operand — and/or return the OBJECT itself (Python identity), not its structure
    29	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       requires truthy(V)
    34	       [priority(40)]
    35	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    36	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    37	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    38	       [priority(40)]
    39	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       requires truthy(V)
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    46	       [priority(40)]

FILE:semantics/str.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))
    42	
    43	  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
    44	  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
    45	  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
    47	  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.
    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
    53	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B
    55	
    56	  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
    59	  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
    60	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule

     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-LIST
     7	  imports MPY-METHODS
     8	
     9	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's tuple case) ======================
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    11	  rule <k> #iterNext(tuple(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, tuple(R)) ... </k>

    13	  // ==== TupleExpr: tuple(ValSeq) literal + == != ===========================
    14	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toTuple"
    15	  rule <k> TupleExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toTuple) ... </k>
    16	  rule <k> #applyK(toTuple, ACC:Vals) => tuple(vals2valSeq(ACC)) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  rule applyCmp("==", tuple(A:ValSeq), tuple(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    19	  // membership routes through the same k-cell fold as lists (list.k)
    20	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     tuple(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, tuple(VS)) ... </k>
    21	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", tuple(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, tuple(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>

    23	  rule applyMethod(tuple(VS:ValSeq), "index", V:Val, .Vals) => idxOfVS(VS, V, 0)

    25	  rule idxOfVS(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), V:Val, I:Int) => I requires A ==K V
    26	  rule idxOfVS(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), V:Val, I:Int) => idxOfVS(R, V, I +Int 1)

    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", tuple(A:ValSeq), tuple(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)

    30	  // ==== target binding: bind a Name or a TupleExpr target to a value ========

    34	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>

    46	       [priority(40)]

    48	  // ==== unpacking: a, b = <tuple|list> (RHS evaluated by strictness) ========
    49	  syntax KItem ::= #unpackSeq(Exprs, ValSeq)
    50	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), tuple(VS:ValSeq)) => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), list(VS:ValSeq))  => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), ref(H:Int)) => Assign(TupleExpr(TS), V) ... </k>

     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)

   104	  rule minVals(M:Int, .Vals)           => M
   105	  rule minVals(M:Int, (I:Int, R:Vals)) => minVals(minInt(M, I), R)

   107	  // ==== bin(n) — "0b" + binary digit codes (promoted from 103's defined fold) ==
   108	  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals) => str(iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(N))))
   109	       requires N >=Int 0
   110	  // negative operand: the '-' sign prefixes the magnitude's digits
   111	  rule applyBuiltin("bin", N:Int, .Vals)
   112	    => str(iCons(45, iCons(48, iCons(98, binCodes(0 -Int N)))))

   114	  syntax IntSeq ::= binCodes(Int) [function, total]
   115	  rule binCodes(0) => iCons(48, .IntSeq)
   116	  rule binCodes(N:Int) => binAcc(N, .IntSeq) requires N >Int 0
   117	  syntax IntSeq ::= binAcc(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
   118	  rule binAcc(0, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
   119	  rule binAcc(N:Int, ACC:IntSeq)
   120	    => binAcc((N -Int pyMod(N, 2)) /Int 2, iCons(48 +Int pyMod(N, 2), ACC))

   123	  // ==== enumerate(xs) — pairs (i, v); materialized eagerly over a list =========
   124	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("enumerate")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))

   126	  syntax ValSeq ::= enumVS(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]

   128	  rule enumVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), I:Int)

   139	  // ==== int(x) identities (int(round(x)) composes through) ====================

   142	  // ==== ord / chr ===========================================================

     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
    77	  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
     2	// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
     3	// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
     4	// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
     5	// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
     6	// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
     7	// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
     8	// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.
     9	
    10	module MPY-SORT
    11	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    12	  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
    13	
    14	  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
    15	  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
    16	  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
    17	  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
    19	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
    20	  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
    21	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    22	  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    23	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]
    24	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R)) requires X  >Int Y [concrete]
    25	  // str elements insert by the shared lexicographic strLt (methods.k)
    26	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSs(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    27	  rule sortVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => insVSs(CS, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    28	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => vCons(str(A), .ValSeq) [concrete]
    29	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(A), vCons(str(B), R))
    30	       requires strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B [concrete]
    31	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(B), insVSs(A, R))
    32	       requires notBool (strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B) [concrete]
    33	
    34	  // sorted(list) constructs a NEW object: k-cell pre-dispatch (beats the [owise]
    35	  // applyBuiltin routing in call.k) so the result allocates.
    36	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
    37	        => #alloc(list(sortVS(VS))) ... </k>
    38	
    39	  // mutator: xs.sort() — the in-place heap write over the same trusted sortVS
    40	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "sort")), .Vals) => noneV ... </k>
    41	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => sortVS(VS)) ... </heap>
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  // ==== keyed / reversed sorted() (WP2) =====================================
    45	  // sortKeyVS(VS, KV): the stable ascending sort of VS by the key value KV
    46	  // (a closure/builtin/type — anything callable). OPAQUE here; the concrete
    47	  // leg (MPY-CONCRETE, llvm only) computes keys by REAL calls and stable-
    48	  // inserts, at priority(40) over these.
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortKeyVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total, symbol(sortKeyVS), no-evaluators]
    50	
    51	  syntax ValSeq ::= revVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    52	                  | revVSAcc(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    53	  rule revVS(S:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(S, .ValSeq)
    54	  rule revVSAcc(.ValSeq, A:ValSeq) => A
    55	  rule revVSAcc(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), A:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(R, vCons(V, A))
    56	
    57	  syntax ValSeq ::= condRev(ValSeq, Bool) [function, total]
    58	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, false) => S
    59	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, true)  => revVS(S)
    60	
    61	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    62	        => #alloc(list(sortKeyVS(VS, KV))) ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    64	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortKeyVS(VS, KV), RB))) ... </k>
    65	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    66	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortVS(VS), RB))) ... </k>
    67	
    68	  // Indexing the opaque sorted list: `valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), I)` is DEFINED because valSeqAt is
    69	  // [total] (subscript.k) — it stays an abstract total value for a symbolic sort and reduces
    70	  // over the concrete sort for krun. No separate sortedAt indirection is needed; wrappers write
    71	  // their postcondition directly as valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), …).
    72	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/concrete.k — MPY-CONCRETE
     2	// Concrete-execution-only rules, visible ONLY to the llvm build (run.sh kompiles
     3	// MPY-CONCRETE; verification builds import MPY and never see these). Rationale:
     4	// a k-cell rule matching value constructors NARROWS abstract Vals in the haskell
     5	// backend ([concrete] is not respected on rewrite rules) — probed on
     6	// 26-remove-duplicates, where element compares branched into deepEqVS.
     7	
     8	module MPY-CONCRETE
     9	  imports MPY
    10	
    11	  // deep equality for list compares whose elements are heap objects
    12	  // (list-of-lists): Python == is structural at every depth.
    13	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("==", list(B:ValSeq))) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    14	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    15	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    16	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("!=", list(B:ValSeq))) => notBool deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    17	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    18	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    19	
    20	  // ==== keyed sort, concrete leg ============================================
    21	  // Computes each key by a REAL call through the uniform #callee machinery
    22	  // (closures, len, type objects all work), stable-inserts on the key, and
    23	  // allocates the result. priority(40) beats sort.k's opaque rules, so krun
    24	  // runs this and proofs (which never see MPY-CONCRETE) keep sortKeyVS.
    25	  syntax Val ::= kvP(Val, Val)
    26	  syntax KItem ::= #ksort(ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    27	                 | #ksIns(Val, ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    29	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, false) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    32	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, RB) ... </k>

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Emit an exhaustive declaration/rule inventory for the audited K sources."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+ROOT = Path("/reference/reference-semantics")
+SOURCES = [ROOT / "semantics.k", *sorted((ROOT / "semantics").glob("*.k"))]
+SOURCES += [Path("/candidate/verification.k"), Path("/candidate/spec.k")]
+
+START = re.compile(
+    r"^\s*(syntax|configuration|rule|context|claim|alias)\b"
+)
+ATTR = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]+)\]")
+
+# Source declarations/rules that participate directly in this submitted
+# program's parse, execution, loop proof, or result. Other supplied rules are
+# still inventoried and inspected, but cannot match this program's reachable
+# terms.
+USED_STARTS: dict[str, set[int]] = {
+    "semantics/syntax.k": {9, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 41, 56, 57, 60, 61},
+    "semantics/core.k": {
+        13, 14, 15, 18, 25, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 49,
+        68, 69, 70, 75, 95, 96, 97, 98, 100, 101, 102,
+        117, 118, 124, 125, 126, 127, 130, 131, 132,
+        157, 158, 185, 186, 189, 190, 191, 194, 195,
+        199, 200, 208, 209, 210, 213, 214, 215, 217, 218, 219,
+    },
+    "semantics/iter.k": {8},
+    "semantics/operators.k": {10, 12, 15, 16, 17},
+    "semantics/int.k": {9, 13, 24, 26},
+    "semantics/str.k": {8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 20, 21, 22, 25},
+    "semantics/list.k": {13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 53},
+    "semantics/tuple.k": {31, 32},
+    "semantics/controls.k": {
+        9, 20, 35, 36, 48, 51, 52, 53, 54, 65, 69, 71, 72, 73,
+    },
+    "semantics/functions.k": {8, 14, 63, 64, 78, 85},
+    "semantics/call.k": {16, 19, 20, 21, 24, 52, 53, 69},
+    "verification.k": {
+        7, 8, 21, 22, 28, 29, 37, 38, 46, 47, 48, 50, 52,
+        55, 56, 58, 59, 60, 62, 65, 66, 68, 71, 72, 74, 76,
+        79, 80, 83, 84, 85, 87, 90, 91, 93, 95, 98, 99,
+        103, 104, 105, 107, 108, 112, 115, 116, 121, 122,
+        123, 125, 127, 129, 132, 133, 135, 136,
+    },
+    "spec.k": {8, 27},
+}
+
+
+def relative(path: Path) -> str:
+    if path.is_relative_to(ROOT):
+        return path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
+    return path.name
+
+
+def classify(path_name: str, line: int, kind: str, text: str, attrs: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    used = line in USED_STARTS.get(path_name, set())
+    if path_name == "verification.k":
+        if kind == "syntax":
+            return "proof-function-declaration", "ACCEPTED_PROOF_DEFINITION"
+        if kind == "rule":
+            return "proof-definitional-equation", "ACCEPTED_PROOF_DEFINITION"
+    if path_name == "spec.k" and kind == "claim":
+        label = "loop-circularity" if "scan-loop" in text else "entry-theorem"
+        return label, "ACCEPTED_MACHINE_CLOSED_CLAIM"
+    if "no-evaluators" in attrs:
+        return "supplied-opaque-symbol", "FIXED_OPAQUE_UNUSED_BY_PROGRAM"
+    if path_name == "semantics/concrete.k":
+        return "supplied-concrete-only", "FIXED_CONCRETE_UNUSED_BY_PROOF"
+    if kind == "syntax":
+        role = "supplied-syntax"
+    elif kind == "configuration":
+        role = "supplied-configuration"
+    elif kind == "context":
+        role = "supplied-evaluation-context"
+    elif kind == "rule" and "<k>" in text:
+        role = "supplied-operational-rule"
+    elif kind == "rule":
+        role = "supplied-equation"
+    else:
+        role = f"supplied-{kind}"
+    decision = (
+        "FIXED_USED_REVIEWED_ACCEPT"
+        if used
+        else "FIXED_NONMATCHING_REVIEWED_ACCEPT"
+    )
+    return role, decision
+
+
+print(
+    "\t".join(
+        [
+            "id",
+            "file",
+            "line",
+            "kind",
+            "attributes",
+            "role",
+            "review_decision",
+            "normalized_declaration",
+        ]
+    )
+)
+
+entry_id = 0
+for source in SOURCES:
+    lines = source.read_text().splitlines()
+    starts = [
+        (index + 1, START.match(line).group(1))
+        for index, line in enumerate(lines)
+        if START.match(line)
+    ]
+    for position, (line_no, kind) in enumerate(starts):
+        next_line = starts[position + 1][0] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines) + 1
+        block_lines = lines[line_no - 1 : next_line - 1]
+        # Do not absorb a module terminator or a new module into the preceding
+        # declaration's display text.
+        display_lines = []
+        for line in block_lines:
+            if line.strip() in {"endmodule"} or line.lstrip().startswith("module "):
+                break
+            display_lines.append(line.strip())
+        text = " ".join(part for part in display_lines if part)
+        attrs = ",".join(ATTR.findall(text))
+        path_name = relative(source)
+        role, decision = classify(path_name, line_no, kind, text, attrs)
+        entry_id += 1
+        safe_text = text.replace("\t", " ")
+        print(
+            "\t".join(
+                [
+                    str(entry_id),
+                    path_name,
+                    str(line_no),
+                    kind,
+                    attrs,
+                    role,
+                    decision,
+                    safe_text,
+                ]
+            )
+        )
*** End Patch

domain theorem: neither the number of groups nor any group length is fixed.

`validInput` accepts sequences containing only `(`, `)`, and ASCII space,
requires nonnegative parenthesis depth at every prefix, permits spaces only at
depth zero, and requires final depth zero. Leading, trailing, and repeated
spaces are also accepted. The result is a fresh list whose entries, in group
order, are the maximum nesting depths. The final environment, stack, return,
exception, heap-location, and exit-code cells are constrained by the target
claim.

## Formal claim

The required target is `SPEC.parse-nested-parens` in `spec.k`:

```k
<k>
  #loadAll(solutionModule)
  ~> Call(Name("parse_nested_parens"), str(CS))
  => ref(0)
</k>
<heap> .Map => 0 |-> list(expectedDepths(CS)) </heap>
...
requires validInput(CS)
```

The claim starts at module loading, resolves the named function through the
fixed environment rules, evaluates the call and exact function body, and
constrains the returned reference and pointed-to list. The auxiliary
`SPEC.scan-loop` claim is a guarded circularity over arbitrary finite suffix
`CS`; fixed semantics executes one loop iteration before the circularity is
reused.

`expectedDepths` is the constructive mathematical contract. `nextDepth`
updates current nesting, `openDeepest` takes the running maximum,
`delimiterOutput` emits a completed nonempty group's maximum, and
`finishOutput` emits the final group. Because `validInput` permits separators
only at depth zero and enforces balanced groups, these equations define exactly

+no additional `requires` condition, and this constructor state is realizable.

+configuration, load the submitted function binding and call it on every finite

+result constraint, not a free variable or implication.

+   have identical digest `94e6b7...baac` and are byte-identical

+
+[inventory_k.py](/audit-output/evidence/inventory_k.py) generated
+[rule-inventory.tsv](/audit-output/evidence/rule-inventory.tsv), SHA-256

+`configuration`, `context`, `rule`, or `claim` across the assembled supplied

+
+| Kind | Count |
+|---|---:|
+| syntax declaration | 246 |
+| ordinary/equational/operational rule | 732 |
+| context | 5 |
+| configuration | 1 |
+| claim | 2 |

+Each row records source/line, complete normalized declaration block,
+attributes (including `function`, `total`, `symbol`, `no-evaluators`,
+`concrete`, `priority`, `owise`, and macros), role, and a review decision.
+There are no proof-local simplification, priority, `owise`, `functional`, or
+opaque declarations. The candidate's 19 proof-local functions are ordinary
+total definitional functions; its only proof extensions beyond those equations
+are the two reachability claims.
+
+### Used construct-to-rule map
+
+| Submitted construct | Supplying declarations/rules and checked behavior |
+|---|---|
+| `Module`, `ImportFrom`, statement sequence | `syntax.k`; `core.k` `#loadAll`/statement sequencing; `controls.k` generic non-math import no-op. The typing import has no runtime effect. |
+| `FuncDef`, `Call`, parameter binding, `Return` | `functions.k` and `call.k`. The named module binding is resolved normally, arguments evaluate left-to-right, a fresh call frame is pushed, and return sets/pops the frame while preserving the returned reference. |
+| locals and `Name` | `core.k` lookup and `controls.k` assignment. The exact current scope is read/written; no closure-cell rule can match the plain frame. |
+| `ListExpr`, reference allocation, `.append` | `list.k`, `core.k`, and `call.k`. The empty list allocates fresh heap location 0; `append` is the mutating-method priority case and updates that same list in place without allocating. |
+| `Str`, string iteration | `str.k` and `iter.k`. ASCII literals map to code sequences, and each `#iterNext` yields a one-character string and the finite suffix. |
+| `For` and loop control | `controls.k`. The iterable is evaluated once; each yield binds `char`, executes the exact body, and returns through the loop label. No body branch contains abrupt return/break/exception. |
+| `If`, `Compare`, truthiness | `syntax.k` strictness, `operators.k`, `str.k`, `int.k`, and `core.k`. Operand order is preserved; equality and integer `>` return booleans; branches use boolean truthiness. |

+

+module environment 0, builtins at -1, call scope 1, heap location 0 for the
+single list, empty stack after pop, `noRet`, `NoExc`, and exit code 0.
+
+### Candidate equations
+
+I checked every [verification.k](/candidate/verification.k) equation:
+
+- `loopBody`, `afterLoop`, `solutionBody`, and `solutionModule` are exact
+  constructor aliases. They replace no program execution; they normalize to
+  syntax before the supplied operational rules run.
+- `nextDepth` partitions character codes into 40, 41, and all others.
+  `scanDepth` consumes exactly one sequence constructor per recursive step.
+- `openDeepest` partitions `D+1 > M` versus `<=`; `delimiterDeepest`
+  partitions `M > 0` versus `<=`; `nextDeepest` has disjoint/exhaustive
+  character cases; `scanDeepest` descends structurally.

+  `nextOutput` has the same exhaustive character partition; `scanOutput`

+  implementation does.

+  string otherwise, matching loop-target binding.
+- `finishOutput` appends the final positive maximum and otherwise leaves output
+  unchanged. `expectedDepths` starts all accumulators at zero/empty.
+- `wellFormedStep` partitions codes 40, 41, 32, and other. Closing and separator
+  cases return false at invalid depths rather than silently assuming validity.
+  `wellFormed` is structurally recursive and checks final depth zero;
+  `validInput` starts at zero.
+

+declared sorts, the guards are disjoint or agree, and recursive calls strictly
+descend on `IntSeq`. No equation is an oracle or contains a task result.
+
+### Loop circularity and state footprint
+
+`SPEC.scan-loop` is a derived reachability lemma, not an operational rewrite.
+Its matched and justified contexts coincide. It executes the fixed
+`#iterNext`, target binding, comparisons, assignments, append, and loop label
+before circular reuse. It reads/writes exactly `depth`, `deepest`, `char`, and
+heap entry `H`; it preserves `paren_string`, `depths=ref(H)`, parent/environment,
+arbitrary continuation, all framed scope/heap entries, allocation counters,
+stack, return state, exception state, and exit code. Since the body has no
+abrupt control, its arbitrary continuation framing is sound.
+
+The claim is universal over arbitrary `D`, `M`, `OUT`, `CH`, and finite `CS`;
+the scanner equations model even non-parenthesis codes consistently. The entry
+theorem later restricts those codes to the contract.
+
+### Supplied opaque and unused rules
+
+The supplied fixed semantics declares the following symbolic primitives:
+`intFloatDiv`, `divII`, `floatMod`, `floatLt`, `absF`, `floorFI`, `toF`,
+`ceilF`, `subF`, `divF`, `addF`, `mulF`, `powF`, `gtF`, `eqF`,
+`decStrToF`, `divFloatIntV`, `intToF`, `truncF`, `roundF`, `roundFN`,
+`sqrtF`, `sortVS`, `sortKeyVS`, and `md5hexCodes`. It also contains
+concrete-only keyed-sort/deep-equality rules. None can occur in the submitted
+program or either proof claim: there are no floats, sorting, MD5, dicts, sets,
+subscripts, comprehensions, or corresponding calls. They do not influence
+control, state, result, or the proof condition here.
+
+All remaining nonmatching supplied rules were inspected and recorded as fixed
+semantics outside this program's reachable term language. No false conclusion
+witness exists on the intended input domain, so I make no unsoundness
+allegation about them. The used supplied rules and every candidate-local rule
+are accepted. In particular, there is no task-answer rule, execution bypass,
+unconstrained result-bearing abstraction, or circular use of an opaque value.
+
+## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test
+
+I inspected the candidate's `spec-vacuity.k` only after completing the
+independent design. The fresh reviewer artifact is
+[false-result.k](/audit-output/evidence/false-result.k).
+
+Its ground input is `"()"` (`40,41`), which satisfies `validInput`; the
+canonical and submitted Python both return `[1]`. The mutation instead demands
+heap result `[2]`.
+
+First:
+
+```text
+kprove false-result.k --definition verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module FALSE-RESULT --dry-run
+```
+
+successfully generated the KORE proof problem and exited 0
+([stage6-false-result-dry-run.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage6-false-result-dry-run.log)).
+The actual proof then exited 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState`; its residual is the
+fully terminated program state with heap
+`0 |-> list(vCons(1,.ValSeq))`, which cannot unify with the demanded `[2]`
+([stage6-false-result-proof.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage6-false-result-proof.log)).
+This is the intended unmet result obligation, not a parse error, missing
+import, timeout, or unrelated crash.
+
+Non-vacuity passes.
+
+## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting
+
+### What the reachability proof establishes
+
+Under the supplied `MPY` definition, for every finite `CS:IntSeq` such that:
+
+- every code is `(` (40), `)` (41), or ASCII space (32);
+- every parenthesis prefix has nonnegative depth;
+- a space occurs only at depth zero; and
+- final depth is zero,
+
+execution of the exact trusted-translated submitted module and named
+`parse_nested_parens` call is partially correct. Its returned reference points
+to a list formed by scanning groups in order, tracking the greatest open depth,
+emitting that value at a separator, and emitting the final group at end. The
+claim also establishes the stated final scope, allocation, stack, return,
+exception, environment, and exit-code cells. The domain is symbolic and
+unbounded in group count, group length, and nesting depth; it is not a finite
+unrolling or examples-only theorem.
+
+For a balanced parenthesis group, the greatest running count of opens minus
+closes is exactly its deepest nesting level. `expectedDepths` is a constructive
+definition of that quantity, and `validInput` ensures separators coincide with
+group boundaries. This is ordinary structural/integer reasoning, confirmed by
+the rule audit and finite differential evidence; it is not an assumed opaque
+answer.
+
+### Trust ledger
+
+| Boundary | Dependents | Assessment |
+|---|---|---|
+| Trusted supplied semantics for the used Python subset | Both claims and concrete K execution | Acceptable benchmark-fixed boundary. Candidate tree is byte-identical to the trusted tree; used rules were statically checked and dynamically exercised. |
+| Trusted `py2mpy.py` | Program identity | Acceptable trusted input. Fresh regeneration is byte-identical; constructor/KORE pinning connects its output to the term executed by the claim. |
+| K v7.1.293 frontend, Haskell/LLVM backends, reachability engine, builtin integer/string/map theories | All machine-checked results | Standard proof-tool trust boundary, explicitly recorded. |
+| CPython 3.10 execution of trusted canonical and submitted Python | Differential evidence only | Finite empirical support, not a proof premise. |
+| English interpretation “balanced nested-parenthesis groups separated by spaces” | Gate-B adequacy | Directly represented by `validInput`; no material contract restriction or fixed bound is introduced. |
+| Supplied opaque float/sort/MD5 primitives | No dependent candidate term or claim | Inert and acceptable here; they are not smuggled into the result. |
+
+Malformed groups, non-ASCII-space separators, and unrelated Python constructs
+are outside the source contract and theorem. Complexity and total termination
+are not separately claimed. Within the requested partial-correctness scope,
+there is no material adequacy, soundness, or auditability gap.
+
+VERDICT: PASS
+LEGITIMACY: LEGIT
*** End Patch

## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks

### Contract and implementation

The trusted [prompt.py](/reference/prompt.py) asks
`parse_nested_parens(paren_string: str) -> List[int]` to take one or more
space-separated groups of nested parentheses and return, in group order, the
greatest nesting depth of each group. Its example maps
`"(()()) ((())) () ((())()())"` to `[2, 3, 1, 3]`.

The trusted [canonical.py](/reference/canonical.py) splits on ASCII space,
ignores empty pieces, and computes each nonempty group's maximum running
parenthesis depth. The submitted [solution.py](/candidate/solution.py) performs
the equivalent single pass on the intended domain: `depth` tracks current
nesting, `deepest` tracks the current group's maximum, and a space emits and
resets a nonempty group's maximum. Leading, trailing, and repeated spaces are
ignored. `()()` is one group with result `1`, which agrees with the canonical
split behavior.

The intended domain consists of balanced groups made only of `(` and `)`,
separated by ASCII spaces. That is what “groups for nested parentheses
separated by spaces” denotes; malformed/unbalanced text and other characters
are not group inputs promised by the prompt. Empty and spacing-only strings
were nevertheless checked as boundaries and both implementations return `[]`.

### Trusted regeneration

In scratch, I ran:

```text
python3 py2mpy.py solution.py > regenerated-solution.mpy
```

The regenerated and submitted files both had SHA-256
`f1320cc5...b3848c` and `cmp` reported byte identity
([stage2-regeneration.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage2-regeneration.log)).
Thus [solution.mpy](/candidate/solution.mpy) is the trusted translator's exact
output for the submitted Python.

### Independent differential test

[differential_test.py](/audit-output/evidence/differential_test.py) imports the
trusted canonical and submitted entry points under separate module names and
uses a separately written prefix-depth oracle. It covers:

- the documented example, empty/spacing-only inputs, one pair, nested pairs,
  adjacent top-level pairs, and leading/trailing/repeated spaces;
- every balanced parenthesis word with one through six pairs (196 groups);
- every ordered pair of those groups with one, two, and three spaces; and
- 27,000 representative three-group cases.

The corpus contained 143,039 unique inputs, digest
`38b903...f1cf9c`, and produced zero canonical/oracle or
candidate/oracle mismatches
([stage2-differential.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage2-differential.log),
exit 0). This finite test supports fidelity and intent; it is not substituted
for the symbolic proof.

## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning

### Claims in plain language

The helper claim [spec.k](/candidate/spec.k) `scan-loop` says: from the exact
supplied-semantics loop state over an arbitrary finite remaining character
sequence `CS`, with locals `depth=D`, `deepest=M`, `depths=ref(H)`, and
`char=CH`, executing the exact `loopBody` finishes the loop, updates those
locals to the scanner summaries, updates heap list `H` to the output summary,
and preserves the framed configuration.

A concrete satisfying helper state is, for example:

```text
CS=.IntSeq, D=0, M=0, OUT=.ValSeq, CH=str(.IntSeq),
L=1, H=7, INPUT=.IntSeq
```

with the exact five-binding scope and heap entry shown in the claim. There is
no additional `requires` condition, and this constructor state is realizable.

The entry claim `parse-nested-parens` says: from the normal initial module
configuration, load the submitted function binding and call it on every finite
`CS` satisfying `validInput(CS)`. If the execution terminates, it returns the
fresh reference `0`; heap location 0 contains
`list(expectedDepths(CS))`; module scope contains the exact loaded closure; the
callee frame is gone; allocation, stack, return, exception, environment, and
exit-code cells have their stated final values. This is an equality-style
result constraint, not a free variable or implication.

Satisfying entry witnesses include `.IntSeq`, `"()"`, and `"(()) ()"`.
`validInput` accepts all of them.

### Constructor-level identity

Program pinning has three independent links:

1. trusted regeneration is byte-identical to submitted `solution.mpy`;
2. reviewer KORE parses of the submitted module and the explicit module term
   have identical digest `94e6b7...baac` and are byte-identical
   ([pinning-expanded.mpy](/audit-output/evidence/pinning-expanded.mpy),
   [stage4-kast-constructor-comparison-attempt2.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage4-kast-constructor-comparison-attempt2.log));
3. the reviewer claim in [pinning.k](/audit-output/evidence/pinning.k) checks
   `solutionModule` against that complete normalized term. It printed `#Top`,
   exit 0
   ([stage4-kprove-pinning-attempt4.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage4-kprove-pinning-attempt4.log)).

The only omitted source information is the type annotation itself; the trusted
translator intentionally renders it as the typing-only `ImportFrom`, and that
import executes as a no-op under the supplied semantics. Every material
operation remains in the executed constructor term.

### Ground substitutions

[ground.k](/audit-output/evidence/ground.k) substitutes the empty input and the
character-code sequence for `"(()) ()"`, constraining the results to `[]` and
`[2, 1]`. It printed `#Top`, exit 0
([stage4-kprove-ground.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage4-kprove-ground.log)).
Both Python implementations also returned `[2, 1]` for that exact input
([stage4-ground-python.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage4-ground-python.log)).

### Actual-body sensitivity

The fresh [body-sensitivity.patch](/audit-output/evidence/body-sensitivity.patch)
changes `Assign(Name("depth"), Int(0))` to `Int(1)` in the
`solutionBody` equation used by `#loadAll`; it does not merely edit an external
Python file. I rebuilt a separate Haskell definition from that changed K source
and ran the unchanged original target. The proof exited 1 with
`WarnStuckClaimState`; the residual contains the mutated closure body and the
unmet equation between `finishOutput(CS,0,0,...)` and execution starting from
depth 1
([stage4-kprove-body-mutation.log](/audit-output/evidence/stage4-kprove-body-mutation.log)).
The theorem is therefore sensitive to the program body it actually executes.

The claim is result-constraining and pins the real regenerated program.

## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review

### Exhaustive inventory

[inventory_k.py](/audit-output/evidence/inventory_k.py) generated
[rule-inventory.tsv](/audit-output/evidence/rule-inventory.tsv), SHA-256
`5e816e...6465`. It inventories every declaration beginning with `syntax`,
`configuration`, `context`, `rule`, or `claim` across the assembled supplied
semantics, all helper K files, `verification.k`, and `spec.k`. There are 986
entries:

| Kind | Count |
|---|---:|
| syntax declaration | 246 |
| ordinary/equational/operational rule | 732 |
| context | 5 |
| configuration | 1 |
| claim | 2 |

Each row records source/line, complete normalized declaration block,
attributes (including `function`, `total`, `symbol`, `no-evaluators`,
`concrete`, `priority`, `owise`, and macros), role, and a review decision.
There are no proof-local simplification, priority, `owise`, `functional`, or
opaque declarations. The candidate's 19 proof-local functions are ordinary
total definitional functions; its only proof extensions beyond those equations
are the two reachability claims.

### Used construct-to-rule map

| Submitted construct | Supplying declarations/rules and checked behavior |
|---|---|
| `Module`, `ImportFrom`, statement sequence | `syntax.k`; `core.k` `#loadAll`/statement sequencing; `controls.k` generic non-math import no-op. The typing import has no runtime effect. |
| `FuncDef`, `Call`, parameter binding, `Return` | `functions.k` and `call.k`. The named module binding is resolved normally, arguments evaluate left-to-right, a fresh call frame is pushed, and return sets/pops the frame while preserving the returned reference. |
| locals and `Name` | `core.k` lookup and `controls.k` assignment. The exact current scope is read/written; no closure-cell rule can match the plain frame. |
| `ListExpr`, reference allocation, `.append` | `list.k`, `core.k`, and `call.k`. The empty list allocates fresh heap location 0; `append` is the mutating-method priority case and updates that same list in place without allocating. |
| `Str`, string iteration | `str.k` and `iter.k`. ASCII literals map to code sequences, and each `#iterNext` yields a one-character string and the finite suffix. |
| `For` and loop control | `controls.k`. The iterable is evaluated once; each yield binds `char`, executes the exact body, and returns through the loop label. No body branch contains abrupt return/break/exception. |
| `If`, `Compare`, truthiness | `syntax.k` strictness, `operators.k`, `str.k`, `int.k`, and `core.k`. Operand order is preserved; equality and integer `>` return booleans; branches use boolean truthiness. |
| `AugAssign` `+`/`-` | `controls.k` and `int.k`. For these local integer names, the old value and evaluated integer RHS produce the exact mathematical update. |
| expression statement | `controls.k`. The `noneV` returned by append is discarded after its heap effect. |

The configuration cells and allocation behavior match the entry postcondition:
module environment 0, builtins at -1, call scope 1, heap location 0 for the
single list, empty stack after pop, `noRet`, `NoExc`, and exit code 0.

### Candidate equations

I checked every [verification.k](/candidate/verification.k) equation:

- `loopBody`, `afterLoop`, `solutionBody`, and `solutionModule` are exact
  constructor aliases. They replace no program execution; they normalize to
  syntax before the supplied operational rules run.
- `nextDepth` partitions character codes into 40, 41, and all others.
  `scanDepth` consumes exactly one sequence constructor per recursive step.
- `openDeepest` partitions `D+1 > M` versus `<=`; `delimiterDeepest`
  partitions `M > 0` versus `<=`; `nextDeepest` has disjoint/exhaustive
  character cases; `scanDeepest` descends structurally.
- `delimiterOutput` appends exactly a positive completed maximum;
  `nextOutput` has the same exhaustive character partition; `scanOutput`
  consumes one character while using the pre-character `M`, exactly as the
  implementation does.
- `scanChar` yields the prior `CH` on an empty suffix and the last one-character
  string otherwise, matching loop-target binding.
- `finishOutput` appends the final positive maximum and otherwise leaves output
  unchanged. `expectedDepths` starts all accumulators at zero/empty.
- `wellFormedStep` partitions codes 40, 41, 32, and other. Closing and separator
  cases return false at invalid depths rather than silently assuming validity.
  `wellFormed` is structurally recursive and checks final depth zero;
  `validInput` starts at zero.

All total functions have exhaustive constructor/guard coverage on their
declared sorts, the guards are disjoint or agree, and recursive calls strictly
descend on `IntSeq`. No equation is an oracle or contains a task result.

### Loop circularity and state footprint

`SPEC.scan-loop` is a derived reachability lemma, not an operational rewrite.
Its matched and justified contexts coincide. It executes the fixed
`#iterNext`, target binding, comparisons, assignments, append, and loop label
before circular reuse. It reads/writes exactly `depth`, `deepest`, `char`, and
heap entry `H`; it preserves `paren_string`, `depths=ref(H)`, parent/environment,
arbitrary continuation, all framed scope/heap entries, allocation counters,
stack, return state, exception state, and exit code. Since the body has no
abrupt control, its arbitrary continuation framing is sound.

The claim is universal over arbitrary `D`, `M`, `OUT`, `CH`, and finite `CS`;
the scanner equations model even non-parenthesis codes consistently. The entry
theorem later restricts those codes to the contract.

### Supplied opaque and unused rules

The supplied fixed semantics declares the following symbolic primitives:
`intFloatDiv`, `divII`, `floatMod`, `floatLt`, `absF`, `floorFI`, `toF`,
`ceilF`, `subF`, `divF`, `addF`, `mulF`, `powF`, `gtF`, `eqF`,
`decStrToF`, `divFloatIntV`, `intToF`, `truncF`, `roundF`, `roundFN`,
`sqrtF`, `sortVS`, `sortKeyVS`, and `md5hexCodes`. It also contains
concrete-only keyed-sort/deep-equality rules. None can occur in the submitted
program or either proof claim: there are no floats, sorting, MD5, dicts, sets,
subscripts, comprehensions, or corresponding calls. They do not influence
control, state, result, or the proof condition here.

All remaining nonmatching supplied rules were inspected and recorded as fixed
semantics outside this program's reachable term language. No false conclusion
witness exists on the intended input domain, so I make no unsoundness
allegation about them. The used supplied rules and every candidate-local rule
are accepted. In particular, there is no task-answer rule, execution bypass,
unconstrained result-bearing abstraction, or circular use of an opaque value.

I inspected the candidate's `spec-vacuity.k` only after completing the
independent design. The fresh reviewer artifact is
[false-result.k](/audit-output/evidence/false-result.k).

Its ground input is `"()"` (`40,41`), which satisfies `validInput`; the

This is the intended unmet result obligation, not a parse error, missing
import, timeout, or unrelated crash.

## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting

### What the reachability proof establishes

Under the supplied `MPY` definition, for every finite `CS:IntSeq` such that:

- every code is `(` (40), `)` (41), or ASCII space (32);
- every parenthesis prefix has nonnegative depth;
- a space occurs only at depth zero; and
- final depth is zero,

execution of the exact trusted-translated submitted module and named
`parse_nested_parens` call is partially correct. Its returned reference points
to a list formed by scanning groups in order, tracking the greatest open depth,
emitting that value at a separator, and emitting the final group at end. The
claim also establishes the stated final scope, allocation, stack, return,
exception, environment, and exit-code cells. The domain is symbolic and
unbounded in group count, group length, and nesting depth; it is not a finite
unrolling or examples-only theorem.

For a balanced parenthesis group, the greatest running count of opens minus
closes is exactly its deepest nesting level. `expectedDepths` is a constructive
definition of that quantity, and `validInput` ensures separators coincide with
group boundaries. This is ordinary structural/integer reasoning, confirmed by
the rule audit and finite differential evidence; it is not an assumed opaque
answer.

### Trust ledger

| Boundary | Dependents | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Trusted supplied semantics for the used Python subset | Both claims and concrete K execution | Acceptable benchmark-fixed boundary. Candidate tree is byte-identical to the trusted tree; used rules were statically checked and dynamically exercised. |
| Trusted `py2mpy.py` | Program identity | Acceptable trusted input. Fresh regeneration is byte-identical; constructor/KORE pinning connects its output to the term executed by the claim. |
| K v7.1.293 frontend, Haskell/LLVM backends, reachability engine, builtin integer/string/map theories | All machine-checked results | Standard proof-tool trust boundary, explicitly recorded. |
| CPython 3.10 execution of trusted canonical and submitted Python | Differential evidence only | Finite empirical support, not a proof premise. |
| English interpretation “balanced nested-parenthesis groups separated by spaces” | Gate-B adequacy | Directly represented by `validInput`; no material contract restriction or fixed bound is introduced. |
| Supplied opaque float/sort/MD5 primitives | No dependent candidate term or claim | Inert and acceptable here; they are not smuggled into the result. |

Malformed groups, non-ASCII-space separators, and unrelated Python constructs
are outside the source contract and theorem. Complexity and total termination
are not separately claimed. Within the requested partial-correctness scope,
there is no material adequacy, soundness, or auditability gap.
